PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: Michael Carter
Age: 56
Sex: Male
Procedure: L3–L5 lumbar fusion with interbody spacers
Surgery date: October 8, 2026
Postoperative day: 1
Primary caregiver: Emily Carter, spouse
Caregiver phone: (202) 555-0143
Care setting: Inpatient surgical unit
SUBJECTIVE
Patient reports lower-back soreness around the surgical site, rated 4/10 at rest and 6/10 during transfers. Reports partial relief after prescribed pain medication. Denies new leg weakness, groin numbness, or loss of bladder or bowel control.
Patient tolerates food and fluids without vomiting. Reports passing gas but has not had a bowel movement since surgery. Voiding after urinary catheter removal.
Spouse is present and plans to assist with meals, transportation, household tasks, and medication organization after discharge.
OBJECTIVE
Vital signs: Temperature 98.6°F; blood pressure 128/76 mmHg; heart rate 78 beats/minute; respiratory rate 16 breaths/minute; oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
General: Alert, oriented, and participating in conversation.
Neurological examination: Lower-extremity strength 5/5 bilaterally in assessed muscle groups. Light-touch sensation intact bilaterally. No new neurological deficit identified in this fictional assessment.
Surgical site: Dressing clean, dry, and intact. No visible drainage through the dressing. Incision not directly inspected during this assessment.
Mobility: Transfers with standby assistance and walks approximately 60 feet using a walker. Requires reminders to avoid twisting during transfers.
ASSESSMENT
Postoperative day one following L3–L5 lumbar fusion with interbody spacers. Incisional pain limits movement but improves with prescribed treatment. No new neurological changes identified. Continued mobility training and discharge education are needed.
CAREGIVER AND HOME ASSESSMENT
Emily Carter is available to remain with the patient during the first 72 hours after discharge. She will drive him home and assist with daily activities.
Home has two entry steps and a bedroom and bathroom on the main floor. Stair training has not yet been completed. Spouse reports concern about assisting with transfers and requests additional instruction.
Patient and spouse prefer written instructions in English. Spouse will participate in discharge teaching with the patient’s permission.
POSTOPERATIVE PLAN
October 9, 2026 — Postoperative Day 1
Continue pain management and neurological monitoring according to surgical-team orders.
Continue physical and occupational therapy for transfers, walking, entry steps, and caregiver training.
Before discharge, confirm the surgeon’s activity restrictions, lifting limit, brace requirements, wound-care instructions, and medication plan. Review the prescribed bowel regimen and monitor urinary and bowel function.
Provide Michael and Emily with follow-up details, the surgical team’s contact information, and instructions for urgent symptoms.
Planned discharge is October 9 at 2:00 PM, contingent on final surgical-team assessment, safe mobility, and completion of caregiver education. Emily will provide transportation home.
